data.title: DBS Raises Over $155 Million By Opening Wealth Strategy to Retail Investors
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat

DBS has raised more than US$155 million from retail investors through a fund based on a strategy previously available only to its wealth clients.

The multiasset DBS Chief Investment Office Barbell Strategy Fund, which raised 200 million Singapore dollars from the new group of investors, is actively managed through market cycles. The strategy it follows has delivered an annualized net return of 7.9% since its inception in 2019, DBS said Monday.

"With this fund, we are extending a flagship strategy previously available only to our wealth clients to a wider group of investors. As market volatility becomes the new norm, we hope to enable our customers to invest consistently with greater confidence as they grow their wealth," DBS Head of Investment Products (Consumer Banking Group) Chua Yi Wen said.

The DBS CIO Barbell Strategy Fund invests in fast-growing stocks in areas such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors and cloud computing, alongside global bonds and alternatives such as gold and hedge funds.

data.title: Hua Medicine Announces Positive Topline Results from U.S. Phase 1b Multiple Ascending Dose Trial of Once-Daily HMS1005
data.description:
Hua Medicine Announces Positive Topline Results from U.S. Phase 1b Multiple Ascending Dose Trial of Once-Daily HMS1005

Hua Medicine Announces Positive Topline Results from U.S. Phase 1b Multiple Ascending Dose Trial of Once-Daily HMS1005

PR Newswire

SHANGHAI, Nov. 22, 2026

SHANGHAI, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hua Medicine (HKEX stock code: 2552) today announced positive topline results from its U.S. Phase 1b multiple ascending dose (MAD) trial of HMS1005, a second-generation glucokinase activator (GKA). The trial enrolled a heterogeneous population of adults (83% White) with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) in the United States. HMS1005 was generally well tolerated across multiple once-daily dose levels. Serum glucose measurements and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) showed improvements in glucose control over the 14-day treatment period.

Dorzagliatin, the world's first GKA, launched in 2022. More than 10 million packs have been used in China to treat T2D patients. Dorzagliatin is designed to restore glucose homeostasis by improving glucose sensing, pancreatic secretory function, GLP-1 secretion and hepatic glucose metabolism. This mechanism, together with the potential for disease modification and drug-free remission, informed the development of a second-generation, once-daily GKA for diabetes and other conditions associated with impaired glucose homeostasis and bioenergy deficiency.

HMS1005 is a second-generation glucokinase allosteric activator and a prodrug of dorzagliatin (HMS5552). Unlike dorzagliatin, which is taken twice daily, HMS1005 is designed for once-daily dosing. The Phase 1b study builds on Phase 1a pharmacokinetic findings, which showed efficient conversion of HMS1005 to dorzagliatin and prolonged systemic exposure.

The Phase 1b study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of HMS1005 in patients with Type 2 diabetes. The study enrolled 48 patients across six cohorts and evaluated once-daily doses ranging from 123 mg to 492 mg. The safety, tolerability, and HMS5552 exposure findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 as a once-daily oral therapy for Type 2 diabetes and related metabolic diseases worldwide.

Key Results

  • Pharmacokinetics: HMS1005 was efficiently converted to dorzagliatin (HMS5552) across all once-daily dose groups (123 to 492 mg). The once-daily extended-release formulation showed a favorable dose–exposure profile for dorzagliatin based on peak concentration (Cmax) and area under the concentration–time curve (AUC), compared with findings from a prior MAD study of twice-daily dorzagliatin. These findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 in Phase 2 trials.
  • Safety and tolerability: HMS1005 was generally safe and well tolerated at doses up to 492 mg once daily. No serious adverse events or episodes of severe hypoglycemia were reported, and no clinically meaningful hypoglycemia (blood glucose below 54 mg/dL or 3.0 mmol/L) was observed. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) showed no increase in time below range (TBR) at once-daily doses of 123 mg to 369 mg. 369 mg was identified as the maximum tolerated dose.
  • Glycemic control: Continuous glucose monitoring showed improvements in glucose management indicator (GMI, an analogous measurement of blood glucose levels to HbA1c) and time in range (TIR). Across the drug tolerant once-daily dose groups from 123 mg to 369 mg, the TIR increased and GMI decreased with active parent drug HMS5552 exposure. The largest observed reduction in GMI was 1.48% in the cohort with high impaired beta-cell function, consistent with observations from dorzagliatin studies. The highest observed TIR increased from approximately 35% at baseline to more than 80% after treatment.

Advantage for once-daily prodrug PK profiles: The pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 as a once-daily extended-release oral therapy. The prodrug HMS1005 and active parent drug HMS5552 exposure profiles support a waiver of long-term GLP toxicity study in the HMS1005 clinical development. If confirmed by the regulatory agency, once-daily dosing second generation GKA development will be greatly accelerated.

Clinical Experience with Dorzagliatin

HMS1005 builds on Hua Medicine's experience with glucokinase activators. Dorzagliatin, marketed in mainland China as HuaTangNing (华堂宁®), has demonstrated glucose-lowering efficacy and a favorable safety profile in previous clinical studies and post-marketing use. HuaTangNing (华堂宁®) has been prescribed to over 600,000 patients in mainland China.

At the 2026 American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions, Hua Medicine presented findings on dorzagliatin from HMM0601, a multicenter post-marketing real-world study involving 2,024 patients with Type 2 diabetes across 80 clinical centers. During the 52-week observation period, no drug-related serious adverse events or episodes of severe hypoglycemia were reported, and the incidence of clinically meaningful hypoglycemia was below 1%. Patients also demonstrated improvements in HbA1c and glycemic control.

At the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes Annual Meeting, further findings from HMM0601 showed that efficacy and safety of dorzagliatin in older adults (aged 65 years or older) and patients with reduced renal function were consistent with those observed in the overall study population.

Interim findings from HMM0701, a prospective real-world observational study, suggested that glucokinase activation may improve TIR and glucose homeostasis in patients with longstanding Type 2 diabetes.

A fixed-dose combination of dorzagliatin and metformin met its pivotal bioequivalence endpoints in recent clinical trials in mainland China. Hua Medicine expects to file a new drug application in 2027.

The clinical experience with dorzagliatin informs the development of HMS1005. Larger, longer trials are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of HMS1005 independently.

Next Steps

Hua Medicine plans to combine data from the Phase 1a and Phase 1b studies with existing clinical and nonclinical data for dorzagliatin to inform discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the HMS1005 development program. Future studies are expected to assess the efficacy and safety of selected once-daily doses over longer treatment periods, including effects on HbA1c and other measures of glycemic control.

Dr. Li Chen, Founder and CEO of Hua Medicine, said, "The Phase 1b results support further development of HMS1005 and build on our experience with glucokinase activators."

"Drawing on our clinical experience with dorzagliatin, we will continue to evaluate whether HMS1005 can improve glucose control with once-daily dosing. We also plan to explore its potential in other indications, including diabetes prevention, prediabetes, and mild cognitive impairment."

Hua Medicine retains all global rights to HMS1005 and plans to engage with potential strategic and financial partners for development outside China.

About Type 2 Diabetes and Glucokinase

According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF Diabetes Atlas, 11th edition), approximately 589 million adults worldwide are living with diabetes, a number projected to rise to 853 million by 2050. Type 2 diabetes accounts for the vast majority of cases. Despite the range of available therapies, many patients do not reach or maintain their blood glucose targets, as the disease progressively erodes the body's ability to sense and respond to changes in blood glucose.

Glucokinase (GK) serves as the body's glucose sensor. Found in the pancreas, liver and gut, it regulates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, hepatic glucose uptake and storage, and the release of incretin hormones such as GLP-1. Impaired glucokinase function is a key defect in T2D. Glucokinase activators (GKAs) are designed to restore this sensing function, addressing an underlying cause of the disease rather than only lowering blood glucose. Hua Medicine's dorzagliatin, approved in China in 2022, is the world's first approved GKA.

About HMS1005

HMS1005 is an investigational new molecular entity and a prodrug of dorzagliatin. It has global patent protection extending to at least 2042. Hua Medicine is developing an extended-release formulation for once-daily oral dosing, with the goal of sustaining glucose control and potentially improving treatment adherence.

About Hua Medicine

Hua Medicine (the "Company") develops and commercializes drugs and is based in Shanghai, China, with companies in the United States and Hong Kong. Hua Medicine works with international partners to develop therapies for unmet medical needs, with a focus on diabetes. Hua Medicine's HuaTangNing (华堂宁®, dorzagliatin tablets) targets the glucose sensor glucokinase, restores glucose sensitivity in patients with Type 2 diabetes, and stabilizes imbalances in blood glucose levels in patients. HuaTangNing was approved by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) of China on September 30, 2022. It can be used alone or in combination with metformin for adult patients with Type 2 diabetes. For patients with chronic kidney disease, no dose adjustment is required. It is an oral glucose-lowering drug that can be used in T2D patients with renal function impairment.

In February 2026, dorzagliatin (trade name: MYHOMSIS®, 華領片®) was approved for marketing by the Pharmaceutical Service of the Department of Health of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

In June 2026, dorzagliatin (trade name: MYHOMSIS®, 華領片®) was approved for marketing by the Pharmaceutical Administration Bureau of the Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

Based on the International Diabetes Federation's 2025 Diabetes Atlas – 11th Edition, there are approximately 148 million diabetic patients in mainland China, 706,000 diabetic patients in Hong Kong SAR, and 52,000 diabetic patients in Macao SAR as of 2024.

Forward-Looking Statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements relating to the business outlook, plans and objectives of Hua Medicine, including statements about the clinical development, regulatory pathway, therapeutic potential, dosing and commercial prospects of HMS1005 and dorzagliatin, the timing of future clinical studies and data disclosures, and potential partnerships. Words such as "anticipate", "believe", "could", "estimate", "expect", "intend", "may", "plan", "potential", "will" and similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements. These statements are based on the current beliefs, assumptions and expectations of the Company's management and are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors, many of which are beyond the Company's control. These include, among others, the uncertainties inherent in clinical development; the possibility that results of earlier studies may not be predictive of results of later studies; the timing and outcome of regulatory submissions and decisions; the Company's ability to secure partners, financing and manufacturing capacity; competition; and changes in market and economic conditions. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied in these forward-looking statements. The forward-looking statements in this press release speak only as of the date of publication and, except as required by applicable law or the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (the "Listing Rules"), the Company undertakes no obligation to update or revise them, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise.

HMS1005 is an investigational product. It has not been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the NMPA or any other regulatory authority, and its safety and efficacy have not been established.

data.title: Creating a new generation of master crafters from the nation's workforce
data.description:
Creating a new generation of master crafters from the nation's workforce

Creating a new generation of master crafters from the nation's workforce

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Nov. 22, 2026

BEIJING, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A report from China Daily.

The All-China Federation of Trade Unions recently released the 2026 list of 200 craftsman academies selected for key support as part of the effort to deepen the reform of the workforce development system and enhance the technical and professional skills of workers.

The academies primarily serve key traditional industries, emerging industries and industries of the future, with a focus on tangible training outcomes and measurable improvements in workers' skills.

Of the 200 academies, 71 percent are affiliated with enterprises, 24.5 percent with vocational schools — including technical institutes — and 4.5 percent were established by trade unions. Together, they have developed 492 distinctive skilled trades covering 19 sectors of the national economy. These skilled trades are concentrated in industries such as information transmission, software and information technology services, and the production and supply of electricity, heat, gas and water, with manufacturing accounting for 55 percent of the total.

The academies offer more than 68,000 in-person courses and have published over 10,000 online skills courses. Since the beginning of this year, they have provided training to more than 1.5 million workers. Among their full-time and part-time instructors, nearly 38,600 are model workers, master craftsmen and other exemplary figures.

Li Shun, a student majoring in intelligent and connected vehicles at Shandong Transportation Craftsman Academy, is one of the beneficiaries of the academy system. "In the intelligent and connected vehicle training laboratory, I learned installation and commissioning technology from a team of master instructors," Li said. "I went from being unable to read circuit diagrams to independently troubleshooting LiDAR faults. I also took part in a field-engineer project at Weichai Power, where hands-on work on the shop floor taught me the true meaning of craftsmanship — paying close attention to every detail."

Li's growth offers an illustration of how Shandong Transport Vocational College cultivates workers for future industries through the spirit of model workers, the spirit of labor and the spirit of craftsmanship. As the first craftsman academy established in China's transportation sector and one of the first such pilot academies set up by a college in Shandong province, Shandong Transportation Craftsman Academy was jointly founded in 2020 by the Shandong provincial transport trade union committee and Shandong Transport Vocational College.

Leveraging the academic strengths of the vocational college and the resource-integration capacity of the trade union, the academy adheres to the principle of "trade union leadership, college-based development and enterprise-centered application". It has built a platform for "nurturing, passing on and promoting craftsmanship", enabling industrial workers to acquire both technical skills and the spirit that sustains them.

By adopting a "master-apprentice" mechanism, the academy has also developed an integrated training platform centered on four functions: skills improvement, innovation incubation, competition and demonstration, and talent cultivation, enabling trainees to hone their capabilities while learning from role models. Over the past few years, the academy has produced a number of technical experts, including Gao Lianjiang, a distinguished craftsman in Shandong's transportation sector, and Shi Jinshui, a recipient of the Shandong May 1 Labor Medal. More than 360 students have also passed the assessment for the title of "Qilu craftsmen".

"In the past, enterprises seeking to cultivate skilled workers often struggled with a lack of qualified instructors and adequate training facilities," said Shen Aibing, head of the training center at Seacon Shipping Group Holdings Limited. "Now, through cooperation with the craftsman academy, we can take part directly in curriculum design, translate job requirements into course content and send our employees here for further training."

According to Shen, the jointly developed training program has cultivated hundreds of technical workers for the company. "The principle of 'enterprise-centered application' brings the power of role models into the workplace, while the spirit of labor has become a driving force behind employees' growth," he added.

In 2024, the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council issued opinions for deeper reform in building the industrial workforce, emphasizing that industrial workers are the principal force of the working class, a key force in creating social wealth and crucial to implementing the innovation-driven development strategy and accelerating the development of China into a high-quality manufacturing power.

During the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-25), the country provided subsidized vocational skills training to over 92 million workers. The number of skilled workers nationwide exceeded 220 million, including over 72 million highly skilled workers. Trade unions cultivated and recognized more than 73,000 craftsmen and craftswomen at various levels and in different fields.

Career development pathways have become clearer. China has explored the establishment of a new eight-level vocational skill grading system. During the 14th Five-Year Plan, more than 44 million workers obtained vocational skills grade certificates, while more than 6,000 technicians were appraised and hired as special technicians or chief technicians.

Workers' incomes have also increased. Efforts have been made to encourage enterprises to conduct collective wage consultations based on skill levels. In 2025, 87,000 collective contracts providing compensation incentives for skilled workers were signed, covering 8.51 million people.

data.title: Asian Equities Fall as AI-Stock Selloff Weighs
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities were lower Monday morning as the selloff in artificial-intelligence stocks outweighed reports of government measures to address the market rout.

The Nasdaq 100, a basket of the largest U.S. technology companies tracked by several tech-oriented investment and retirement funds, flirted with bear-market territory on Friday, closing at 25028.98, a nearly 20% fall from its record high last month.

"The latest sell-off reflects growing concerns over stretched technology valuations, the scale and financing of AI-related capital expenditure, and uncertainty over the returns on these investments," Commerzbank Research analysts said in a report. "Stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue guidance from a leading U.S. chipmaker in its latest quarterly earnings report failed to reassure investors."

South Korea's Kospi slipped 3.8%, with chip-making index heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics falling 3.5% and 4.5%, respectively. Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index dropped 1.0% and Malaysia's FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI shed 0.6%. Japan's markets were closed for a public holiday.

However, the regional stock selloff could be limited by reports of Asian government measures to address the market rout.

"Chinese authorities moved to ease margin requirements to 80% from 100% buying securities with borrowed funds, South Korea announced some phased measures including ensuring a stock stabilization fund is in place to respond when needed, and Taiwan widened curbs on short sales of local stocks," said Taylor Nugent, senior economist at National Australia Bank, in a commentary.

Oil declined amid prospects for resilient global supply conditions.

Shipments of oil through major Middle Eastern chokepoints rose 19% in the third quarter from the prior three months, according to a report published last week by the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The agency said regional crude production reached 23.1 million barrels a day in October, the highest since the conflict began, as producers expand shipments through alternative routes.

"Monthly crude oil flows out of the Middle East have ranged between 80%-90% of pre-war levels in October," said John Oh, an analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, in a report. "We estimate that oil flows out of the Middle East only need to average 60%-70% of pre-war levels to keep global oil inventories unchanged. Therefore, current flows out of the Middle East should see global oil inventories build."

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures fell 0.3% to $83.13 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures were 0.5% lower at $92.10 a barrel, according to ICE data.

data.title: LG ELECTRONICS' ULTRAVIEW WINDSHIELD DISPLAY WINS 2026 AUTOMOTIVE NEWS PACE PILOT AWARD
data.description:
LG ELECTRONICS' ULTRAVIEW WINDSHIELD DISPLAY WINS 2026 AUTOMOTIVE NEWS PACE PILOT AWARD

LG ELECTRONICS' ULTRAVIEW WINDSHIELD DISPLAY WINS 2026 AUTOMOTIVE NEWS PACE PILOT AWARD

PR Newswire

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 22, 2026

Award Recognizes LG's Context-Aware Approach to In-Vehicle Information as Company Advances Validation with Global Automakers

News Summary

  • LG Electronics has won the 2026 Automotive News PACE Pilot Award for its UltraView Windshield Display, a solution that presents driving information and infotainment content across a large area of the windshield.
  • The solution adjusts screen size and information density to suit driving conditions, reducing the need for drivers to shift their gaze between the road and multiple cockpit displays.
  • UltraView Windshield Display combines a compact, focus-free augmented reality head-up display (AR-HUD) with LG's proprietary Hover HUD, showing information at different virtual distances so drivers can check it with less need to refocus their eyes.
  • LG is conducting vehicle-level proof-of-concept evaluations with global automakers and plans to explore opportunities for future production programs.

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics (LG) has won the 2026 Automotive News PACE Pilot Award for its UltraView Windshield Display, an in-vehicle display solution that shows driving information and infotainment content across a large area of the windshield.

Presented by Automotive News, the PACE Pilot Award recognizes early-stage automotive innovations that are not yet commercialized but have demonstrated their potential through pilot programs. LG's win highlights its approach to organizing information within the driver's field of view.

Rethinking In-Vehicle Information Delivery

As vehicles add more digital functions and connected services, the amount of information presented to drivers keeps growing. With driving data, navigation, entertainment and vehicle controls often spread across multiple displays, drivers may need to shift their gaze between the road and different screens more frequently.

Rather than adding more screens or expanding display size, LG developed UltraView Windshield Display to rethink how, when and where information reaches the driver. The solution organizes information by importance and driving context, supporting a more intuitive driving experience. This reflects LG's broader vision for next generation automotive displays, which shifts the focus from individual display devices to a more integrated and context-aware information experience.

Bringing Context-Aware Information to the Windshield

UltraView Windshield Display combines a compact, focus-free AR-HUD with LG's proprietary Hover HUD in a single optical system, presenting different types of visual data at distinct virtual distances. The AR-HUD projects driving-critical information, including vehicle speed, advanced driver assistance system (ADAS) alerts, and navigation cues, at a far virtual distance aligned with the road. Its focus-free design reduces the difference in focal distance between the road and the projected image, so drivers can check information more naturally while keeping their eyes on the road. Meanwhile, the Hover HUD displays navigation, vehicle status, climate controls and multimedia content on a large virtual screen that appears closer to the driver.

Together, these two technologies allow UltraView Windshield Display to adjust screen size and information density to driving conditions, helping drivers access relevant information while minimizing unnecessary shifts in visual attention. Its compact design also gives automakers greater flexibility in cockpit design and display configuration.

Advancing Toward Real-World Vehicle Applications

LG has been conducting vehicle-level proof-of-concept evaluations of UltraView Windshield Display with multiple global automakers, including premium brands in Europe and Asia. These collaborations include vehicle-level validation and sourcing discussions, and vehicle demonstrations and technology showcases have drawn further inquiries from automakers. Building on this progress, LG plans to further validate the technology for real-world vehicle applications and explore opportunities for future production programs.

"Winning the Automotive News PACE Pilot Award recognizes our approach to rethinking how information is delivered inside the vehicle," said Eun Seok-hyun, president of the LG Vehicle Solution Company. "We will build on this recognition by working closely with automakers to bring new display experiences from innovation to real-world mobility."

About LG Electronics Vehicle Solution Company

The LG Vehicle Solution Company (VS) is bringing LG's unique mobility innovations to the automotive industry. As a trusted and innovative partner, the company provides intelligent solutions including head units, displays, connectivity, ADAS vision systems, and software solutions integrating human-centered AI and automotive engineering into the modern AI/software-defined vehicle. Committed to "Driving better future mobility," the company has diversified its portfolio to further strengthen its capabilities, including automotive lighting systems, e-powertrain and cybersecurity. For more information, visit www.LG.com/global/mobility. To stay updated with the latest news, subscribe to the LG mobility newsletter, LG Loop at www.LG.com/global/mobility/newsletter and follow the LG VS Company LinkedIn channel at www.linkedin.com/company/lgvehiclesolution.

data.title: BHSI Names Lloyd Haynes Head of Casualty, Asia
data.description:
BHSI Names Lloyd Haynes Head of Casualty, Asia

Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance (BHSI) today announced that it has appointed Lloyd Haynes as Head of Casualty, Asia, based in Singapore.

In his new role, Lloyd will lead BHSI’s Casualty business across Asia, working closely with underwriting teams to deepen relationships with brokers and customers and expand BHSI’s presence across the region.

“We are delighted to welcome Lloyd to BHSI and our team in Asia,” said Marcus Portbury, President, Asia Middle East, BHSI. “Lloyd’s experience underwriting complex Casualty risks and his strong market relationships make him an excellent addition to our team. We look forward to working with Lloyd as we continue to strengthen our Casualty offering across Asia.”

Lloyd is based in BHSI’s Singapore office and can be reached at Lloyd.haynes@bhspecialty.com

In Asia, BHSI offers a broad range of Casualty solutions, including general liability, products liability, excess and umbrella liability, employer’s liability, and tailored coverage for construction and energy risks.

Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance Company (incorporated in Nebraska, USA) provides commercial property, casualty, healthcare professional liability, executive and professional lines, transactional liability, surety, marine, travel, programs, accident and health, employer stop loss, homeowners, and multinational insurance. Zepp Health Corporation Reports Third Quarter of 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

Zepp Health Corporation Reports Third Quarter of 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

PR Newswire

MILPITAS, Calif., Nov. 22, 2026

MILPITAS, Calif., Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zepp Health Corporation (NYSE: ZEPP) ("Zepp", the "Company" or "we") today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial and Operating Highlights:

  • Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%.
  • Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments.
  • GAAP and adjusted net loss[1] attributable to Zepp were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million in the same period of 2025, and US$11.3 million and US$12.5 million in the second quarter of 2026. The net loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities.
  • As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million as of September 30, 2025 and US$106.3 million as of June 30, 2026.
  • Product Innovation: Launched T-Rex Dual Solar, pairing a bright AMOLED display with solar charging through both the front of the watch and its glass-ceramic back. It offers up to 25 days of battery life under typical use, and its dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation are designed for multi-day trips outdoors.
  • Software Ecosystem: Rolled out Zepp OS 6 to more existing watch models and made HYROX post-race station analysis available on more models. These updates give customers more value from the devices they already own and help build confidence in Amazfit's ongoing support for its products.

[1] Adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation represents net income/(loss) excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss) and (vii) tax effects of the above non-GAAP adjustments. See "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

"The third quarter was a period of adjustment for us," said Wayne Huang, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Zepp Health. "Tight supply for some of our core products weighed on revenue, while unfavorable exchange rates and higher prices for memory and other chips put pressure on gross margin. The adjustments we made across our products, training software, supply, and retail are already beginning to pay off in the fourth quarter, and we are heading into the holiday season and the year ahead with momentum.

In the third quarter, global activations across the Balance family rose approximately 40% from the second quarter, driven by our new, higher-priced models. Combined global activations for Active 3 Premium and Active Max, our two US$169 models, grew approximately 35% over the same period. We also expanded our premium outdoor lineup with T-Rex Dual Solar, a watch priced at about US$650 that pairs a bright AMOLED display with dual-sided solar charging and offline navigation for multi-day trips. Through Zepp OS 6 and HYROX updates, we brought new training tools to more watches that customers already own, giving them more value from their devices.

Product availability has started to improve in some markets in the fourth quarter, including for T-Rex 3. We have also made it easier for customers to compare watches in stores. At REI, we provided materials to help shoppers compare models. Large screens are now in place at our Amazfit counters in select Best Buy stores. They make the counters easier to spot and show shoppers how our devices fit into everyday activity, training, and recovery. As more products reach store shelves, we believe we will be better positioned to meet holiday demand."

Leon Deng, Chief Financial Officer of Zepp Health, commented, "Third-quarter revenue reached US$68.3 million, up 7.5% sequentially and within our guidance range. While revenue declined 9.9% year-over-year, we continued to see encouraging momentum in our Active series. Supply constraints on certain higher-margin products, including Balance 3 and Helio Strap, limited our ability to fully capture market demand during the quarter.

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 37.4% in the previous quarter and 38.2% in the same period last year, reflecting unfavorable foreign exchange movements, continued increases in memory component costs, and supply constraints on our higher-margin products. Importantly, excluding the tariff-related benefit recorded in the second quarter, our underlying gross margin remained strong sequentially. Continued improvement in our product mix helped offset a meaningful portion of these external cost pressures, demonstrating the progress we have made in strengthening our premium product portfolio and underlying unit economics.

We continued to balance financial discipline with targeted investments to support future growth. On a sequential basis, adjusted operating expenses decreased to US$34.2 million, and adjusted operating loss narrowed to US$10.3 million. The year-over-year increase in operating expenses was primarily driven by strategic investments in new product launches, brand building, athlete partnerships, and distribution expansion. At the same time, general and administrative expenses declined, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency and manage our structural cost base.

We ended the quarter with US$99.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, while inventory declined to US$68.6 million from US$87.7 million a year earlier. We also continued to strengthen our balance sheet by extending our debt maturity profile, converting an additional US$26.6 million of short-term borrowings into longer-term obligations during the quarter. We remain committed to returning value to shareholders through our ongoing share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, we had cumulatively repurchased US$17.8 million under our US$20 million authorization, and our board of directors recently approved a one-year extension of the existing program.

Looking ahead, we expect fourth-quarter revenue to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 6% to 12%. As product availability improves and our expanded distribution channels begin contributing more meaningfully, we remain focused on translating our investments into stronger revenue growth and greater operating leverage. Despite near-term external cost pressures, we believe our improving product mix, disciplined cost management, and continued investment in the Amazfit brand are building a stronger foundation for sustainable long-term growth and profitability."

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%. The year-over-year decline was due to the broader macroeconomic environment and a strong comparison base, as well as supply constraints on top-selling offerings, particularly Helio Strap and Balance 3. However, revenue from the Active series increased significantly year-over-year.

Gross Margin

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, supported by new product introductions including the Active series, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments. Gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 benefited from tariff refunds that the Company recorded related to duties previously remitted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"). Excluding the impact of these refunds, gross margin increased sequentially.

Research and Development Expenses

Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$11.4 million, compared with US$10.8 million and US$11.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Excluding US$0.6 million of foreign currency headwinds, research and development expenses were flat compared with the same period of 2025. We continued to invest in a series of cutting-edge products as well as new technologies, including AI, to maintain our competitive edge against our peers. At the same time, we focused on refined research and development approaches, consistently evaluating resource efficiency to optimize return on investment and productivity.

Selling and Marketing Expenses

Selling and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$18.0 million, compared with US$12.0 million and US$18.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. The US$6.0 million year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to US$1.9 million investment across online and offline channels for content refreshes, in-store displays and holiday season readiness, and US$1.5 million of launch campaigns for new products including the Balance 3, Balance Ultra and T-Rex Dual Solar. The remainder of the increase reflected US$1.4 million for marathons, Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) and media sponsorships, and US$1.2 million related to the HYROX and new athletes partnerships.

General and Administrative Expenses

General and administrative expenses were US$5.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$7.0 million and US$6.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. We continued to streamline overhead, maintaining disciplined cost control while improving operating efficiency.

Operating Expenses

GAAP and adjusted operating expenses[2] for the third quarter of 2026 were US$35.0 million and US$34.2 million, respectively, compared with US$29.8 million and US$28.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and US$36.0 million and US$34.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Out of the year-over-year increase of US$5.2 million in operating expenses, US$0.8 million was due to foreign currency impacts. The remaining US$4.4 million was primarily due to higher selling and marketing expenses as mentioned above. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, operating expenses decreased slightly.

Operating Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted operating results[3] were loss of US$11.1 million and loss of US$10.3 million, respectively, compared with loss of US$0.9 million and income of US$0.4 million in the same quarter of 2025. The net operating loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities, but the operating loss narrowed compared with the second quarter of 2026. 

Net Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted net loss attributable to Zepp for the third quarter of 2026 were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with GAAP and adjusted net loss of US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million for the same quarter in 2025. The US$10.9 million year-over-year increase in adjusted net loss was primarily driven by a US$6.0 million increase in selling and marketing expenses, as discussed above, followed by a US$3.2 million unfavorable foreign exchange impact. In addition, higher memory and other component costs resulted in a net US$2.7 million gross profit headwind, partially mitigated by a more favorable product mix. These unfavorable impacts were partially offset by US$1.1 million in savings from general and administrative expenses.

[2] Adjusted operating expenses represent operating expenses excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Please refer to the section titled "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

[3] Adjusted operating income/(loss) represents operating income/(loss) excluding: (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. See "Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash were US$99.0 million, compared with US$102.6 million and US$106.3 million as of September 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026, respectively.

The Company recorded inventory of US$68.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with US$62.4 million as of June 30, 2026 and US$87.7 million as of September 30, 2025. We will continue to manage the inventory level tightly and working capital closely.

Long-term and short-term debt levels remained flat as of September 30, 2026 compared with June 30, 2026. We remain committed to prudently managing our debt profile. Our primary objective is to maintain overall debt levels broadly stable while actively extending the maturity profile by replacing short-term borrowings with long-term debt. During the third quarter and for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we successfully converted US$26.6 million and US$56.5 million, respectively, of short-term debt into long-term obligations, and we expect to continue this strategy in the coming quarters, supported by sufficient financial headroom and liquidity capacity. Since the beginning of 2023, the Company has cumulatively retired US$38.1 million of debt, and will continue to optimize its capital structure.

Share Repurchase Program Update

The Company announced in its third quarter 2021 earnings release that the board had authorized a share repurchase program of up to US$20 million through November 2022. On November 21, 2022, the board authorized a 12-month extension of the Company's share repurchase program. On November 20, 2023, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. On November 18, 2024, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 24 months. On November 22, 2026, the board further authorized the Company to extend its share repurchase program for another 12 months. Pursuant to the extended share repurchase program, the Company may repurchase its shares in the form of ADSs and/or ordinary shares through November 2027 with an aggregate value equal to the remaining balance under the share repurchase program. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had used US$17.8 million to repurchase approximately 2.4 million ADSs. The Company expects to fund the repurchases under the extended share repurchase program out of its existing cash balance.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company's management currently expects net revenues to be between US$90.0 million and US$95.0 million, which would represent an increase by approximately 6% to 12% from US$85.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2025.

This outlook is based on current market conditions and reflects the Company's current and preliminary estimates of market, operating conditions and customer demand, which are all subject to change.

About Zepp Health Corporation

Zepp Health (NYSE: ZEPP) is the technology company behind Amazfit, a global sports technology brand. Its wider portfolio includes Zepp Clarity hearing technology and Zepp Aura sleep and recovery services.

The company's vertically integrated technology platform brings together Zepp OS, wearable chipsets and biometric sensors designed in-house, and algorithms for biometric measurement and personalized guidance to enhance product performance and user experiences across devices, software and services.

Zepp Health operates as a global multi-hub organization, bringing together R&D, product, design, brand and business expertise across the Americas, Europe and Asia. These teams co-create and share responsibility for innovation, product performance and global growth.

Founded in 2013, Zepp Health has shipped more than 200 million units of smart wearable devices, with products available in more than 90 countries. Its principal office is in Gorinchem, the Netherlands. For more information, visit: www.zepp.com

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

We use adjusted net income/(loss), a non-GAAP financial measure, in evaluating our operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes. Adjusted operating expenses represent operating expenses excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Adjusted operating income/(loss) represents operating income/(loss) excluding: (i) share-based compensation expenses and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements. Adjusted EBIT represents net income/(loss) excluding (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss), (vii) income tax (benefit)/expense, and (viii) interest income and interest expense. Adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation is a non-GAAP measure, which excludes (i) share-based compensation expenses, (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from acquisitions and business cooperation agreements, (iii) gain/(loss) from fair value change of long-term investments, (iv) impairment loss from long-term investments, (v) income/(loss) from equity method investments, (vi) investment income/(loss), and (vii) tax effects of the above non-GAAP adjustments, and is used as the numerator in computation of adjusted net income/(loss) per share and per ADS attributable to Zepp Health Corporation.

We believe that adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation help identify underlying trends in our business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain expenses that we include in net income/(loss) and net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation. We believe adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation provide useful information about our operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making.

Adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to Zepp Health Corporation, should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to net income/(loss), basic and diluted net income/(loss) per share and per ADS attributable to Zepp Health Corporation or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating performance. Investors are encouraged to review the historical non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measures. Adjusted EBIT and adjusted net income/(loss) attributable to ordinary shareholders, presented here may not be comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to our data. We encourage investors and others to review our financial information in its entirety and not rely on a single financial measure.

data.title: FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. ("FFR") Becomes Approved Robotics Supplier to Top-Tier U.S. Public School Districts, Forms Strategic Partnerships with School Districts, and Fulfills Their Robot Orders
data.description:
FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. ("FFR") Becomes Approved Robotics Supplier to Top-Tier U.S. Public School Districts, Forms Strategic Partnerships with School Districts, and Fulfills Their Robot Orders

FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. ("FFR") Becomes Approved Robotics Supplier to Top-Tier U.S. Public School Districts, Forms Strategic Partnerships with School Districts, and Fulfills Their Robot Orders

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 22, 2026
  • FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. ("FFR") is now an approved robotics supplier to a top-tier California public school district and has joined its procurement platform which means more than 1,000 schools in the district can now purchase FFR robots and its education productivity solutions directly.
  • The Company recently welcomed Carolyn Kissane as an independent director on FFR's board. As associate dean of NYU's Center for Global Affairs, she brings deep experience connecting academia, research, and industry. Her expertise will help expand FFR's robotics education ecosystem, strengthen partnerships, engage more developers, and accelerate its Four-Core Full-Stack AI strategy across all four industry ecosystems.
  • Last week, FFR launched in Dubai, introducing six robots to the Middle East. With local partners, it showcased real-world applications across education, security, entertainment, healthcare, and interactive sports, marking a new chapter for Physical AI in the region.
  • FFAI reported its Q3 results last week and achieved a major milestone in financial governance. As of September 30, 2026, management concluded that all nine previously identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting had been remediated and that related controls were operating effectively which will help build a stronger foundation for its businesses.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR) ("FFR" or the "Company"), a U.S.-based Embodied AI ("EAI") robotics company, today shared a weekly business update from YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF and FFR.

"Welcome to my 82nd weekly report. Let me start with three major breakthroughs for FFR's education ecosystem in U.S. K–12 and career education. First, FFR is now an approved robotics supplier to a public school district that is considered top-tier both nationally and within California. We've cleared the district's review and joined its procurement platform. That means more than 1,000 schools in the district can now purchase FFR robots and our education productivity solutions directly. This week, the district's career education center led the way by purchasing several robots, including FX Navi and Aegis EDU. We hope the project will serve as a model for a broader rollout across the district.

Second, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with another public school district, one of California's leading districts. The district has also purchased robot devices including Master Mini and Aegis EDU. Third, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with an additional major public school district in Los Angeles.

The second and third partnerships both cover K–12 through adult education. We'll work with the two districts to develop curricula together, set up innovation labs, create career and technical education pathways, train teachers, and give students hands-on experience. Together, we'll explore how Physical AI education can connect what students learn in the classroom with further study, real-world practice, and career development. These two collaborations both renew automatically at the end of their terms. With these frameworks in place, we can move future projects forward quickly through a streamlined process.

Outside of California, we are also moving forward with strategic partnerships and sales in robotics education across multiple school districts in four other states: New York, Pennsylvania, Florida, and Texas. FFR pioneered K–12 robotics education in the U.S., and we're now No. 1 in the industry. The progress we've made on strategic partnerships and robot purchases across these three leading districts matters to FFR and to the whole industry. Let me share four reasons why:

First, it's a big step forward for our education ecosystem. By working with major school districts as strategic partners at the school district level, we can work directly with the U.S. public education system to build Physical AI education pathways that connect K–12 learning, technical skills training, and future careers.

Second, these projects give us a model for replicating at scale nationwide. The U.S. has more than 13,000 regular public-school districts. Across the country, about 130,000 public and private K–12 schools serve roughly 53 million students. That's a large market, with opportunities across robot devices, curricula, teacher training, and ongoing services. We'll learn from our first projects with leading districts, turn what works into a repeatable model, and gradually roll it out to across the country.

Third, it helps us move faster on our Four-Core Full-Stack AI business in education and speeds up the evolutionary flywheel. In real classrooms, we can deploy robot devices, develop Skills and solutions, and collect data in line with applicable requirements. That data helps us keep improving our Education Brain.

Fourth, it helps transform U.S. education in the Physical AI era. By making robots a regular part of teaching and hands-on learning, we can prepare the next generation of developers and skilled workers for the new era. As FFR's profile in the industry grows, we've received invitations from schools, universities, and school districts to take part in academic discussions and major exhibitions. I'll share more about those with you in future reports.

Regarding corporate governance, this week, we welcomed Carolyn Kissane to FFR's board as an independent director. Carolyn is the associate dean of New York University's Center for Global Affairs. She brings years of experience in higher education and knows how to bring universities, researchers, and companies together. Carolyn could help us grow our robotics education ecosystem, reach more developers, and build more industry partnerships. She'll also help us bring technology, talent, industry, and capital together. That will help us put our Four-Core Full-Stack AI strategy to work faster across all four industry ecosystems.

We also held our Middle East launch in Dubai this week. Six of our robots made their debut in the region. With our local partners, we showed five ways to put robots to work across our four industry ecosystems: education, security and inspection, entertainment, healthcare, and interactive sports. Together, we're opening a new chapter for Physical AI in the Middle East. We'll share a video from Dubai next week, so stay tuned.

For FFAI: it released its Q3 results this week. I want to highlight an important step we've taken on financial management and internal controls. After evaluating and testing the controls, FFAI management concluded that, as of September 30, 2026, FFAI had corrected all nine previously identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting. Management also concluded that the related controls were operating effectively. FFAI has spent nearly two years improving FFAI's financial management and internal controls. This progress puts us in a stronger position to meet our obligations as a public company, raise capital, and rebuild trust with investors. It also gives us a stronger foundation to grow and create value through our shared Robotaxi network, AI VisiCabin operations, and Physical AI investment and holdings business. All right, thanks for tuning in. I'll see you next week!"

About FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. 
FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR) is a U.S.-based Embodied AI robotics company focused on the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization and deployment of intelligent robotic technologies, products and industry solutions. FFR is building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of Physical AI Brain & Developer Platform, Physical AI Devices, Physical AI Industry Productivity Solutions, and Physical AI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, All Robots, Multi-capabilities," FFR aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified Physical AI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The ecosystem is designed to support the full robotics lifecycle, including R&D, deployment, data collection and training, operations, and commercial applications. FFR also operates RoboShare, a robot-sharing and services platform. To learn more, visit https://www.ff.com.
